references.text: Isaiah prophesied that the Messiah would have his grave with a rich man: 'They made his grave with the wicked, but with the rich in his death' ([ref:Jes 22:16|Isaiah 22:16]) – a reference to a tomb carved out of rock.

Isaiah's prophecy about the suffering servant: 'They made his grave with the wicked, but with the rich in his death' ([ref:Jes 53:9|Isaiah 53:9]). The fulfillment is seen in that Joseph of Arimathea, a rich man, laid Jesus' body in his own new tomb.
Matthew's parallel account of the burial: Joseph wrapped the body in clean linen and laid him in his new tomb which he had carved out of rock ([ref:Matt 27:59-60|Matthew 27:59-60]).
Mark's parallel account: Joseph bought fine linen, took Jesus down, wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a tomb that was carved out of rock ([ref:Mark 15:46|Mark 15:46]).

John's account of Jesus' burial, where Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus laid Jesus' body in a new tomb in a garden, where no one had yet been laid ([ref:Joh 19:38-42|John 19:38-42]). John also emphasizes that the tomb was new, corresponding to Luke's remark that no one had yet been laid there.
John specifies that the tomb was new and that 'no one had yet been laid in it' ([ref:Joh 19:41|John 19:41]), which corresponds directly with Luke's description 'where no one had yet been laid'.

The immediate context: Joseph of Arimathea, a good and righteous man, went to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body ([ref:Luk 23:50-52|Luke 23:50-52]). This explains who performed the action described in verse 53.
Paul refers to Jesus' burial in his speech in Antioch: 'When they had finished all that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb' ([ref:Apg 13:29|Acts 13:29]).
Paul confesses as part of the central gospel that 'Christ was buried' ([ref:1 Kor 15:4|1 Corinthians 15:4]), which Luke 23:53 is the historical account of.
